headline: Approved zoning changes for accessory dwelling units, parking, and Class VI roads; postponed Pillsbury Road development agreement.
summary: Residents spoke about the Stokes Road bridge, a Veterans Tax Credit increase, and investigations into the former town manager. By consensus, the Town will pause reallocations on the Hall Road bridge while NHDOT completes an alternatives analysis. A DPW facility master plan update and a Planning Board resignation were also covered.
decisions: Accepted the resignation of Lieutenant Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board, 5-0.
Approved zoning amendments on accessory dwelling units, residential parking, and development on Class VI highways and private roads, 5-0.
Agreed by consensus to pause reallocations on the Hall Road bridge, await NHDOT's alternatives analysis, and hold a joint public hearing in January 2027.
Postponed the Off-Site Improvement Agreement with PE Realty Partners to November 9, 2026.
Postponed the Capital Improvements Plan presentation to a future agenda with no date set.
Approved the October 19, 2026 Town Council meeting minutes, 5-0.

Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 1 
Londonderry Town Council Meeting Minutes 
Monday, November 2, 2026 | 7:00 p.m.  
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Londonderry Town Hall 
Council Members Present: 
Chair Ron Dunn 
Vice Chair Shawn Faber 
Councilor Dan Bouchard 
Councilor Deb Paul 
Councilor Ted Combes 
Council Members Absent: 
None 
 
Meeting Video Link: 
http://173.166.17.35/internetchannel/show/14381?
channel=4 
Other Staff Present: 
Acting Town Manager Kim Alan Bernard 
Finance Director Justin Campo 
Director of Public Works Dave Wholley 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen 
Director of Planning & Economic Development Jacob 
LaFontaine 
Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee 
Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis 
Division Chief of Fire Prevention Brian Johnson 
Minutes Prepared By: 
Kirsten Hildonen using Gemini Notebook AI 
A. CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Dunn called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Councilor 
Bouchard requested a moment of silence for Gerry Van Grievenhoff, a lifelong Londonderry 
resident who served 20 years with the school district lunch program, 10 years as a crossing guard 
at North School, 37 years as Supervisor of the Checklist, and was deeply devoted to the Leach 
Library. 
Vice Chair Faber announced the completion of the independent investigation, reporting that 
allegations of bullying and intimidation against the former town manager were substantiated. He 
expressed support for town employees and stated that the Council is committed to enforcing 
strict anti-harassment policies to ensure a respectful workplace environment across municipal 
operations. 
Councilor Ted Combes addressed accusations previously made against him by the former town 
manager, noting that the final investigation report cleared him of any legal or charter violations. 
He reaffirmed his focus on supporting municipal staff and serving the residents of Londonderry. 
B. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment:
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 2 
Name: Joe Paradis 
Address: 16 St. Andrews Way 
Presented on behalf of the Londonderry Veterans Banners Committee regarding the Veterans 
Flag/Banner Initiative to honor local military veterans with light pole banners across town. 
Name: Nancy Hendricks 
Address: 14 King John Drive 
Reported receiving a trustee resignation and outlined the board's planned search process to select 
a replacement. She assured the Council that the library board would complete the candidate 
vetting and interviewing before bringing a formal recommendation to the Council for final 
appointment. 
Name: Tara Myles 
Address: 11 Lancaster Dr 
Commended Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard for demonstrating grace and leadership during a 
turbulent period for Town government. She sharply criticized Council members for ongoing 
political bickering and lack of decorum, urging them to act professionally and focus on key town 
priorities like paving roads and economic development. 
Name: Tim Porter 
Address: 14 Quentin Dr 
Speaking as an individual Londonderry taxpayer, School Board member Tim Porter addressed 
Question 2 on the local ballot regarding a proposed cap on the school district's tax levy. He argued 
that the cap is misleading and does not lower overall property taxes, warning that it could create 
budget deficits that force cuts to classroom instruction and student services. 
Name: Sarah Faber 
Address: 73 Old Nashua Road 
Questioned Councilor Paul regarding an alleged conflict of interest involving municipal payments 
to her newspaper, asking how much the Town paid to the paper last year. She also criticized the 
former town manager's history of internal investigations, asserting that Councilors Paul and 
Bouchard previously supported a $50,000 IT budget addition for staff surveillance cameras and 
promoted a proposed ethics policy that functioned as a power grab. 
Councilor Bouchard stated that Ms. Faber’s time was up and that Vice Chair Faber had stopped 
the clock three times for her. Finance Director Campo stated that from 1 Nov 2025 to 1 Nov 
2026, the Town paid $7,304 to the Londonderry Times.  
Name: Jane Cooper 
Address: 73 Winterwood Dr 
Inquired about where residents could access the first independent investigation report, which 
Chair Dunn confirmed was published on the Town website. She also requested clarification 
regarding executive compensation, prompting confirmation that the Acting Town Manager 
receives a $1,500 weekly stipend in addition to his police chief salary. 
Name: Richard Bielinski 
Address: 89 Hall Road
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 3 
Questioned the Fire Chief’s 5.5% salary increase after four and a half months on the job, asking 
whether raises should follow the LEEA contract's July 1 schedule or the anniversary date specified 
in his signed offer letter. He expressed concern over altering voter-approved pay scales without a 
new warrant article and called for a thorough review of municipal compensation adjustments to 
ensure transparency. 
Name: Moira Ryan 
Address: 2 Snowberry Hollow 
Requested that the Council take necessary steps to increase Londonderry's optional Veterans Tax 
Credit from $750 to $1,000 pursuant to newly enacted state legislation. Councilor Combes 
clarified that while the vote can occur sooner, the statutory effective date for tax bills is April 1, 
2027. 
Name: John Perez 
Address: 5 Wesley Drive 
Criticized the Council majority for ordering a second investigation into former Town Manager 
Shaun Mulholland after the initial report cleared him, raising questions about unrecorded 
interviews, procedural flaws, and his termination prior to the second report's completion. She also 
condemned the decision to exclude two Council members from executive proceedings, warning 
that the majority's lack of transparency and teamwork exposed the town to costly litigation. 
Name: Kathleen 
Address: Londonderry, NH 
Inquired regarding the attorney fees and if they were going to be broken down into categories and 
asked when it would be available. Chair Dunn confirmed the next bill would be itemized. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
Councilor Bouchard raised concerns regarding the Council Chair’s authority and whether certain 
actions complied with the Town Charter, including compensation authorized for the Acting Town 
Manager. He also questioned the authorization of an annual airport-related stipend and requested 
clarification regarding who approved it and whether a Council vote occurred. Councilor Bouchard 
further raised concerns about the October 26 attorney-client meeting, the subsequent release of 
investigative reports, and the process surrounding the investigations. Discussion followed among 
Council members regarding the nature of the October 26 meeting, whether a vote had been taken, 
pending litigation, and what matters could appropriately be discussed publicly. 
C. BOARD APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS 
1. Resignation of Lieutenant Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board. 
The Council considered the resignation of Lieutenant Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board. 
Councilor Combes moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the resignation of 
Lieutenant Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board with sincere appreciation for his service to the town. 
Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 4 
D. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
1. Receive public input, discuss, and approve proposed Zoning Ordinance amendments 
relating to Accessory Dwelling Units under RSA 674:71-73, Residential Parking under 
RSA 674:16, VII, and Development on Class VI Highways and Private Roads under RSA 
674:41. 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen and Director of Planning and Economic 
Development Jacob LaFontaine presented proposed amendments to the Londonderry Zoning 
Ordinance recommended by the Planning Board following public hearings on September 2, 2026. 
The amendments align local regulations with 2025 state legislative updates effective in 2026, 
including establishing a minimum of one off-street parking space per residential unit (RSA 674:16, 
VII), updating frontage provisions on Class VI highways and private roads (RSA 674:41), and 
updating dimensional, design, and parking standards for attached and detached Accessory 
Dwelling Units (RSA 674:71–73) developed with the Southern New Hampshire Planning 
Commission under a Housing Opportunity Planning Grant. 
Councilor Combes moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Chair Dunn asked for public comment. There was none. 
Vice Chair Faber moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 5-
0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the proposed amendments 
to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance relating to Accessory Dwelling Units pursuant to RSA 674:71–
73, Residential Parking pursuant to RSA 674:16, VII, and Development on Class VI Highways and 
Private Roads pursuant to RSA 674:41, as recommended by the Planning Board on September 2, 2026, 
and as presented. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
2. Receive public input and discuss the funding, purpose, and proposed design of the 
Stokes Road Bridge project, including its coordination with the anticipated New 
Hampshire Department of Transportation (NHDOT) realignment of Routes 28 and 128. 
Director of Public Works Dave Wholley and Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis 
presented an update regarding the Stokes Road Bridge project, Municipal State Aid Bridge 
Funding (80/20 split), state Red List bridge classifications (Stokes Road and Hall Road), and 
coordination with NHDOT's upcoming realignment of the Routes 28 and 128 (Rockingham Road 
and Mammoth Road) intersection. NHDOT previously approved swapping State Aid Bridge 
funding from Stokes Road to Hall Road due to Hall Road's critical transportation and emergency 
service impact. 
State Senator Sharon Carson (19 Tokenel Road, NH Senate President) addressed the Council 
regarding constituent concerns from Stokes Road residents and emphasized state level 
coordination.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 5 
Councilor Bouchard moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Chair Dunn asked for public comment: 
Name: Robert Demers 
Address: 18 Stokes Road 
Clarified that he shared a concern, not a complaint. Discussed bridge vs. culverts options, 
neighborhood notice timing, road safety, traffic speed, and emergency vehicle access. 
Division Chief of Fire Prevention Brian Johnson addressed emergency vehicle access, response 
times, and secondary access routes. 
Name: Janet Huttula 
Address: 5 Stony Point Drive 
Spoke from personal experience regarding commercial customer access and traffic patterns along 
the Stokes Road corridor, and the visible damage on the bridge. 
Councilor Paul recused herself at 8:48 p.m. 
Name: Dave Martin 
Address: 4 Stokes Road 
Stated that there is no room for a cul-de-sac or to widen the road. Pointed out that the work to 
realign the 28/128 intersection is likely ten years away. 
Councilor Combes moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-0-
0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Senator Carson presented some additional information on the state of the Stokes Road bridge and the 
financial breakdown for work on the two bridges. Deputy Director Danis suggested that it would be 
best to wait until after the first of the year to make any decisions because more information will be 
available them. 
Councilor Combes moved to reopen the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion 
carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Name: Robert Demers 
Address: 18 Stokes Road 
Asked where the funding to remove the bridge would come from if they waited for the 
intersection project. 
Name: Chris Halla 
Address: 14 Stokes Road 
Raised concerns regarding project delays since 2023, road safety, and neighborhood 
communication. 
Name: Janet Huttula 
Address: 5 Stony Point Drive 
Stated that this is a safety problem right now that needs to be dealt with now.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 6 
Councilor Combes moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-0-
0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Council discussion followed between Councilors Combes, Faber, Dunn, Bouchard, and Paul. By 
Council consensus, the Town will pause reallocations on the Hall Road bridge, await NHDOT's 
alternatives analysis (expected Dec 2026/Jan 2027), hold a joint public hearing with the NHDOT 
Commissioner in January 2027, and maintain active communication with Stokes Road 
neighborhood residents. 
Councilor Paul rejoined the meeting at 9:33 p.m. 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. Discuss and authorize the Town Manager to execute the Off-Site Improvement 
Agreement with PE Realty Partners (Procopio). 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen and Attorney Laura Gandia (Devine Millimet, 
representing Procopio) presented the proposed Off-Site Improvement Agreement for the PE 
Realty Partners (Procopio) development at 36 and 44 Pillsbury Road within the Woodmont 
Commons Planned Unit Development (PUD). The agreement defines developer obligations for 
public infrastructure, roadway improvements, signage, pavement markings, and traffic 
management associated with the 250 single-family cottage units (Thornton Hill) and 60 
condominium units conditionally approved by the Planning Board on April 8, 2026. 
Councilors Paul and Bouchard raised questions regarding the timing of document distribution and 
legal review. Councilor Bouchard invoked Councilor's Privilege under Town rules to allow 
additional time to review agreement documents. 
Item postponed under Councilor's Privilege to the November 9, 2026 Town Council meeting. 
2. Receive a presentation from the DPW Working Group and the Owners Project 
Manager (OPM) firm and the architect on the work done to date. 
Director of Public Works Dave Wholley, Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis, School 
Board Chair Bob Slater, Owner's Project Manager PMA Consultants, and architectural consultant 
Weston & Sampson delivered a comprehensive presentation on the DPW Facility Master Plan. 
The presentation reviewed key milestones since the establishment of the DPW Facilities Working 
Group under Resolution 2025-18 and extension under Resolution 2026-15 through April 2028. 
Topics included facility site evaluations at 120 High Range Road, site tours, CIP submittals, 
community outreach events (Old Home Day, Senior Expo, Household Hazardous Waste Day on 
Nov 21), expended ARPA feasibility funds ($64,500), PMA contract ($74,472), Weston & Sampson 
design support ($37,500), and the target March 2028 municipal ballot vote for 30% design 
development ($150,000 in FY28) toward a 50-year modernized public works facility ($30M–
$50M). The team officially launched the project website. 
3. Receive a presentation of the Capital Improvements Plan.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 7 
This item was postponed to a future agenda with a date to be determined. 
F. OLD BUSINESS 
None. 
G. APPROVAL OF CONSENT ITEMS 
1. Town Council meeting minutes from October 19, 2026 
Councilor Combes moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by Vice Chair 
Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
H. OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Liaison Reports 
None. 
2. Town Manager Report 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard recognized the work put into the Procopio agreement with 
the staff, clarified the police chief airport stipend history dating back to 2007 and that COLA and 
merit increases do not apply to this stipend, and forecasted the work put into the upcoming 
budget presentations. 
I. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Bob Slater 
Address: Chair, School Board 
Expressed concerns that employee names were not redacted in the investigation reports that 
were released. Asked the Council to move forwards and work to ensure that staff are protected. 
Name: Janet Huttula 
Address: 89 Hall Road 
Inquired regarding Councilors Deb Paul and Dan Bouchard's statements concerning former Town 
Manager Shaun Mulholland, citing reported workplace stress experienced by municipal staff. 
Addressing Councilor Paul directly regarding town legal records, Hudela stated that confirmation 
from the State Attorney General's office indicated the documents are public information, and 
questioned why standard procedures for accessing public records were not utilized. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
Councilor Paul expressed frustration that Chair Dunn permitted personal attacks from the 
podium. Clarifying her position, Councilor Paul stated she was not defending Mulholland—noting
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 2, 2026 
Page 8 
she had frequently clashed with him publicly herself—but was objecting strictly to the Council 
majority's process and the exclusion of two councilors from executive decision-making. 
J. NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
None held. 
K. ADJOURNMENT 
Vice Chair Faber moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. 
Chair votes in the affirmative. The meeting adjourned at 11:13 p.m. 
L. MEETING SCHEDULE 
• November 7, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 10:00 a.m. (FY2028 Initial Budget 
Presentation) 
• November 9, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 6:00 p.m. 
• November 16, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 6:00 p.m.
